governance: Subject identity precedes relic object, reported custody and map pin.
Popular versus obscure remains unassessed until liturgical, historical and local-cult evidence is researched.
Traditional three relic classes and significant/non-significant ecclesiastical categories are separate dimensions.
Reported relic custody does not authenticate an ancient attribution.
The census is a partial source-indexed sampling, not a claim to all relics worldwide.
Legacy objects remain as references; no new production map pins.

notes: Case-study conflict retained: Monte Cassino describes Saint Benedict's remains; Fleury also has a historically attributed Saint Benedict relic claim in the legacy registry. Do not automatically merge distinct relic objects or authenticate both claims.
One subject may have multiple object claims and one place may hold multiple relics. The separate source-provenance and access distinctions are preserved.
Blesseds Daudi Okello and Jildo Irwa are not described as canonized saints.
Historical tomb memorials do not by themselves establish that identifiable bodily relics remain in place.
A source-screened claim is not an ecclesiastical certification of authenticity or a full provenance chain.
